design.text: 48-week multicenter study (Core Period) with a 12-week open-label dose titration, a 12-week open-label maintenance, an 8-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal period (which provided the primary endpoint data), and an open-label Period 4.

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of ISTURISA was assessed in a 48-week, multicenter study (called the Core Period) that consisted of four study periods as follows:
Period 3: 8-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal treatment period which provided the data for the primary efficacy endpoint

population.text: Cushing's disease patients with persistent or recurrent disease despite pituitary surgery, or de novo patients for whom surgery was not indicated or who refused surgery; mean age 41 years, 77% female.

citations.quote: The trial enrolled Cushing's disease patients with persistent or recurrent disease despite pituitary surgery or de novo patients for whom surgery was not indicated or who had refused surgery. The mean age at enrollment was 41 years; 77% of patients were female.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: percentage of complete responders (mUFC ≤ ULN) at the end of the 8-week randomized withdrawal period (Week 34), comparing continued ISTURISA versus placebo.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint of the study was to compare the percentage of complete responders at the end of the 8-week randomized withdrawal period (Period 3) between patients randomized to continue ISTURISA versus the patients switched to placebo.

n.text: 137 patients received ISTURISA in Period 1; 71 responders were randomized 1:1 at Week 26 to continue ISTURISA (n=36) or switch to placebo (n=35).

citations.quote: 137 patients received a starting dose of 2 mg ISTURISA orally twice daily
At Week 26, 71 patients were considered responders and were randomized 1:1 to continue receiving ISTURISA (n = 36) or to switch to placebo (n = 35) for 8 weeks.

result.text: At end of Period 3, complete responder rate was 86% (ISTURISA) vs 29% (placebo); difference 57% (95% CI 38, 76); 2-sided p<0.001. Key secondary complete responder rate at Week 24 was 52.6% (95% CI 43.9, 61.1).

citations.quote: At the end of Period 3, the percentage of complete responders for the primary endpoint was 86% and 29% in the ISTURISA and placebo groups, respectively (Table 3). The difference in percentage of complete responders between ISTURISA and placebo groups was 57%, with 95% two-sided CI of (38, 76).
The key secondary endpoint, complete responder rate after 24 weeks of treatment with ISTURISA was achieved by 72/137 patients (52.6%) with 95% two-sided CI of (43.9, 61.1).

indication.text: ISTURISA is a cortisol synthesis inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative.

target_moa.text: Osilodrostat is a cortisol synthesis inhibitor that inhibits 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1), the enzyme responsible for the final step of cortisol biosynthesis in the adrenal gland; it also inhibits aldosterone synthase.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) in the 48-week study (N=137) were adrenal insufficiency (43.1%), fatigue (38.7%), nausea (37.2%), headache (30.7%), edema (21.2%), and nasopharyngitis (19.7%). Key risks include hypocortisolism, QT prolongation, and accumulation of adrenal hormone precursors/androgens.
